source_evidence.observation: The standing problem is Ax = b with A in R^{n x n} nonsingular and 0 != b in R^n; the right preconditioner M_R is nonsingular. The surrounding text assigns preconditioner applications to u_m, products with A to u_a, and remaining GMRES work to u_g, and introduces flexible GMRES as persistently storing Z_k = [z_1,...,z_k]. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, equations (1.1)-(1.2) and paragraph introducing Algorithm 1.)

The right branch computes z_j = M^{-1}v_j in u_m, w_j = Az_j in u_a, MGS and the least-squares coefficients in u_g, y'_k = V_k y_k in u_g, and x_k = x_0 + M^{-1}y'_k in u_m. The text below states that this study fixes M_R for all iterations. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1 and following paragraph.)

The paper invokes the standard floating-point model, defines fl(.) as a computed value, treats c(n,k) as unspecified low-degree polynomials, uses lesssim and approximately-equal after dropping negligible second-order terms, defines the vector 2-norm and matrix Frobenius and induced 2-norms, uses an undifferentiated kappa when norm distinctions are unnecessary, and defines relative forward error by ||hat{x}-x||_2/||x||_2. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2 and equation (2.1).)

Algorithm 2 represents the search-space basis by tilde{Z}_k, while the discussion distinguishes it from the computed basis hat{Z}_k and says the difference is technical and used in the appendices. The least-squares process uses MGS, Givens rotations, and a triangular solve. (PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Section 3.1 and Algorithm 2.)

The modular result supplies an existential dimension k <= n, with the selected computed Krylov basis satisfying sigma_min(hat{V}_k)^{-1} <= 4/3 and sigma_max(hat{V}_k) <= 4/3, and gives the generic forward-error estimate later specialized in Theorems 3.3 and 3.4. (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1 and equations (3.7)-(3.8).)

Equation (3.14) models each computed right-preconditioner application, equation (3.15) defines rho_A^R from the computed basis and coefficients, equation (3.16) gives five smallness requirements, and Theorem 3.3 asserts existence of k <= n with the three-term right-preconditioned forward-error bound (3.17). (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.14)-(3.17) and Theorem 3.3.)

Flexible GMRES uses a fixed M_R, stores hat{Z}_k explicitly, computes the solution directly by a u_g matrix-vector product with hat{Z}_k, and does not reapply M_R^{-1}. Theorem 3.4 assumes the complete condition (3.16), asserts existence of k <= n, and gives the two-term bound (3.20); Remark 4 identifies the omitted u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) term. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Section 3.4, Theorem 3.4, equation (3.20), and Remarks 4-5.)

The proof models the A product by |Delta A^{(j)}| lesssim c(n,k)u_a|A| and defines tilde{z}_j = hat{z}_j + A^{-1}Delta A^{(j)}hat{z}_j, thereby absorbing this rounding error into the mathematical search space and setting epsilon_c = 0. It explicitly says tilde{Z}_k is not algorithmically accessible. (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, Appendix C, equations (C.1)-(C.2).)

After explicitly dropping second-order terms, equation (C.3) expands right-preconditioned solution formation through a u_g product with hat{V}_k followed by a fresh u_m application of M_R^{-1}. Equations (C.7)-(C.10) propagate the A-product perturbation through rho_A^R and relate computed and mathematical search-space products. (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, Appendix C, equations (C.3)-(C.10).)

Equation (C.11) bounds the solution-formation perturbation by c(n,k)(u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) + u_g kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R)||tilde{Z}_k hat{y}_k||_2 and identifies the corresponding epsilon_x; the proof also has epsilon_b = 0 because M_L = I. (PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, Appendix C, equation (C.11) and following paragraphs.)

source_evidence.anchor: Appendix C conclusion and Appendix D, equation (D.1)
source_evidence.observation: Appendix C invokes Theorem 3.1 to obtain an existential k <= n and derives (3.17). Appendix D replaces right-preconditioned solution formation by hat{x}_k = fl(hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k) = (hat{Z}_k + Delta Z_k^{(3)})hat{y}_k with |Delta Z_k^{(3)}| lesssim c(n,k)u_g|hat{Z}_k|. (PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, conclusion of Appendix C and Appendix D, equation (D.1).)

source_evidence.anchor: Appendix D, equation (D.2) and recovery of (3.20)
source_evidence.observation: Equation (D.2) contains only the u_g kappa(M_R) and u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R contributions to the local solution-formation error. The proof states that avoiding preconditioner reapplication spares u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), then substitutes the new epsilon_x into (3.8) to recover (3.20). (PDF p. 45, printed p. 44, Appendix D, equation (D.2) and final paragraph.)

binders: The standing exact problem is Ax = b with A in R^{n x n} nonsingular, 0 != b in R^n, and exact solution x = A^{-1}b in R^n. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, equation (1.1).)

M_R in R^{n x n} is a nonsingular right preconditioner and M_L = I; in the flexible case M_R^{(j)} = M_R != I for every j <= k. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, equation (1.2); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, opening of Section 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, opening of Section 3.4.)

u_m, u_a, and u_g denote the relevant floating-point arithmetics or their unit roundoffs: u_m for applying M_R^{-1}, u_a for multiplying by A, and u_g for the remaining GMRES operations. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, paragraph introducing Algorithm 1; PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)

For j <= k, hat{v}_j is a computed Krylov vector, hat{z}_j = fl(M_R^{-1}hat{v}_j), hat{Z}_k = [hat{z}_1,...,hat{z}_k] in R^{n x k}, hat{y}_k in R^k is computed from the GMRES least-squares problem, and hat{x}_k is the computed solution. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.14)-(3.15).)

The conclusions quantify existentially over an iteration k satisfying k <= n, rather than asserting the bounds at every iteration. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4.)
hypotheses: Each computed preconditioner application satisfies fl(M_R^{-1}hat{v}_j) = (M_R^{-1} + Delta M_R^{(j)})hat{v}_j with ||Delta M_R^{(j)}||_F <= c(n,k)u_m eta_R||M_R^{-1}||_F for j <= k, where eta_R is a scalar measuring application error. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.14).)

For right-preconditioned GMRES, products AM_R^{-1}hat{v}_j are executed by applying M_R^{-1} in u_m and then A in u_a; the solution is formed by a u_g product with hat{V}_k followed by a fresh u_m application of M_R^{-1}. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Section 3.3; PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1, lines 6-18.)

The complete applicability condition is max(u_g kappa(AM_R^{-1}), u_g kappa(M_R), u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R, u_a kappa(AM_R^{-1})kappa(M_R)) << 1. No one of these five displayed requirements may be omitted from Theorem 3.3's stated hypothesis. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.16) and Theorem 3.3.)

Flexible-preconditioned GMRES uses the same product model (3.14), the same complete condition (3.16), and a fixed preconditioner M_R^{(j)} = M_R for all j <= k, but forms the solution directly from stored hat{Z}_k in u_g. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Section 3.4 and Theorem 3.4.)
The analysis uses the standard floating-point model and assumes the relevant unit roundoffs are substantially below 1. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)
conclusions: Right-preconditioned conclusion: there exists an iteration k <= n such that ||hat{x}_k-x||_2/||x||_2 lesssim c(n,k)(u_g kappa(AM_R^{-1})kappa(M_R) + u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R). (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3 and equation (3.17).)

Flexible-preconditioned conclusion: under the same condition (3.16), there exists an iteration k <= n such that ||hat{x}_k-x||_2/||x||_2 lesssim c(n,k)(u_g kappa(AM_R^{-1})kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R). (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4 and equation (3.20).)

The flexible displayed bound omits the additive u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) contribution because the stored computed preconditioned basis is used directly and M_R^{-1} is not reapplied during solution formation; the full applicability condition (3.16), including its u_m terms, nevertheless remains a hypothesis. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Remark 4 and Theorem 3.4; PDF p. 45, printed p. 44, equation (D.2).)
definitions_and_conventions: rho_A^R := || |hat{Z}_k| |hat{y}_k| ||_2 / ||hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k||_2, with hat{Z}_k = [hat{z}_1,...,hat{z}_k] and hat{z}_j = fl(M_R^{-1}hat{v}_j) for j <= k. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.14)-(3.15).)
The relative forward error is ||hat{x}-x||_2/||x||_2, where x is exact and hat{x} is computed. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, equation (2.1).)

fl(.) denotes a computed floating-point value; hats denote computed quantities, whereas tilde{Z}_k is a mathematical search-space basis introduced to absorb selected rounding errors and is not algorithmically accessible. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Section 3.1; PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, equation (C.2).)
eta_R is not a precision: it is a scalar quantifying the magnitude of error in applying the right preconditioner. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, text following equation (3.14).)
c(n,k) denotes unspecified low-degree polynomials in the dimension n and iteration count k. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)

The symbols lesssim and approximately-equal are used after negligible second-order terms have been dropped, so the displayed conclusions are asymptotic rounding-error bounds rather than exact inequalities with a stated numerical constant. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)
implicit_context: There is no left preconditioner: M_L = I, so the preconditioned right-hand side equals b and incurs no computation or epsilon_b contribution. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Section 3.3; PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, paragraph following equation (C.11).)

Theorems 3.3 and 3.4 specialize the modular Theorem 3.1, which supplies an existential k <= n and a well-conditioned computed Krylov basis at that k. (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, Theorem 3.1 and equation (3.7); PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, conclusion of Appendix C.)

The GMRES variant uses Modified Gram-Schmidt; the least-squares implementation is described as MGS followed by Givens rotations and a triangular solve. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Section 3.1.)

With the right preconditioner fixed, right- and flexible-preconditioned GMRES are mathematically equivalent in exact arithmetic, although their floating-point solution-formation paths differ. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, paragraph following Algorithm 1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, opening paragraphs of Section 3.4.)

The displayed algorithm and theorem use one sequence indexed through k <= n; no restart parameter or restarted-cycle conclusion is stated. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3.)
statement.algorithm_linkage: Algorithm 1's right branch computes hat{z}_j = fl(M_R^{-1}hat{v}_j) in u_m, applies A in u_a, performs MGS and the least-squares work in u_g, computes hat{V}_k hat{y}_k in u_g, and then reapplies M_R^{-1} in u_m. Flexible GMRES persistently stores the computed hat{z}_j vectors and instead forms the final correction directly as hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k in u_g, with no final preconditioner reapplication. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, paragraph introducing flexible GMRES; PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Section 3.4.)
numerical_model: The paper uses the standard floating-point model with u_m, u_a, and u_g interpreted as unit roundoffs in the error formulas. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)
Preconditioner application is normwise modeled in Frobenius norm by ||Delta M_R^{(j)}||_F <= c(n,k)u_m eta_R||M_R^{-1}||_F. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.14).)

The A product is modeled componentwise by |Delta A^{(j)}| lesssim c(n,k)u_a|A|, and its error is absorbed into tilde{z}_j = hat{z}_j + A^{-1}Delta A^{(j)}hat{z}_j. (PDF p. 41, printed p. 40, equations (C.1)-(C.2).)

For right preconditioning, the proof expands hat{x}_k = fl(M_R^{-1}hat{V}_k hat{y}_k) after dropping second-order terms; the resulting local solution-formation parameter is c(n,k)(u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) + u_g kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R). (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, equation (C.3); PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, equation (C.11).)

For flexible preconditioning, hat{x}_k = fl(hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k) = (hat{Z}_k + Delta Z_k^{(3)})hat{y}_k with |Delta Z_k^{(3)}| lesssim c(n,k)u_g|hat{Z}_k|; its local parameter is c(n,k)(u_g kappa(M_R) + u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R). (PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, equation (D.1); PDF p. 45, printed p. 44, equation (D.2).)

The fixed operator M_R does not imply fixed rounding perturbations: equation (3.14) permits an application-dependent Delta M_R^{(j)}. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.14); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, fixed-preconditioner statement.)
error_notions: The claimed quantity is relative forward error in the original system Ax = b, not residual error, backward error, or error in the preconditioned variable. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, equation (2.1) and opening of Section 3.)

The bound is attainable and existential: it holds at at least one iteration k <= n under the hypotheses, not uniformly for every k. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4.)

The right-preconditioned bound separates a u_g contribution, a preconditioner-reapplication contribution proportional to u_m eta_R, and an A-product contribution proportional to u_a rho_A^R. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17); PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, equation (C.11).)
The flexible bound retains the u_g and u_a rho_A^R contributions but has no explicit additive u_m eta_R term. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20) and Remark 4.)
norms: The forward error and rho_A^R use the vector 2-norm; for matrices, ||.||_2 is the induced 2-norm. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2 and equation (2.1); PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)
The application-error model (3.14) uses the matrix Frobenius norm. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.14).)
The paper defines kappa_F, kappa_2, and kappa_{F,2}, then writes generic kappa(B) when it does not differentiate among these equivalent normwise quantities. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)

The numerator of rho_A^R is the 2-norm of the product displayed as |hat{Z}_k||hat{y}_k|, preserving cancellation sensitivity relative to ||hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k||_2. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15); PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, equation (C.7).)
constants_and_indexing: The witness iteration satisfies k <= n exactly; the theorem does not use k < n or k <= n+1. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4.)

The computed preconditioned basis has columns indexed j = 1,...,k, while Arnoldi also forms v_{j+1} and h_{j+1,j}. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1, lines 5-14; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)
rho_A^R is iteration-dependent because both hat{Z}_k and hat{y}_k depend on k. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)
The multiplicative c(n,k) is not numerically specified; only its status as a low-degree polynomial is guaranteed. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2.)

The proof's cross-referenced modular witness uses the explicit constants 4/3 in equation (3.7), while intermediate lower bounds use a leading 3/4 before small perturbations; these constants do not appear as explicit factors in final bounds (3.17) or (3.20). (PDF p. 9, printed p. 8, equation (3.7); PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, equation (C.13); PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, equation (C.15).)
higher_order_terms: The symbol lesssim in the theorem bounds signals that negligible second-order terms have been dropped. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation convention; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)
Appendix C explicitly says it drops second-order terms when expanding the right-preconditioned solution-formation path in equation (C.3). (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, equation (C.3).)

The smallness assumptions in (3.16) are used in the proof to discard products of perturbation terms and certify the modular applicability conditions. (PDF p. 42, printed p. 41, equations (C.4)-(C.10); PDF p. 43, printed p. 42, equations (C.11)-(C.14).)

Neither final theorem supplies an explicit Big-O remainder, coefficient for the omitted terms, or exact value of c(n,k). (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation convention; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)
exceptional_values: A is nonsingular and b != 0, so the exact solution x is nonzero and the denominator ||x||_2 in the relative forward error is nonzero. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, equation (1.1); PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, equation (2.1).)

M_R is nonsingular, making M_R^{-1} and AM_R^{-1} well-defined; the flexible section additionally states M_R != I. (PDF p. 3, printed p. 2, equation (1.2); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, opening of Section 3.4.)

Equation (3.15) does not explicitly state that ||hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k||_2 is nonzero, so rho_A^R is not defined by the displayed ratio if that denominator vanishes. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)

The selected passages invoke the standard floating-point model but do not separately specify behavior for overflow, underflow, subnormals, NaNs, infinities, or Arnoldi breakdown. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1.)

undebatable_constraints: Both results concern right or flexible right preconditioning of a nonsingular n-dimensional system and assert existence of an iteration k <= n. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, Theorem 3.3; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4.)
The full five-entry maximum in equation (3.16) is the stated hypothesis for both Theorem 3.3 and Theorem 3.4. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.16); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4.)

The right-preconditioned bound has exactly the three displayed first-order sources u_g kappa(AM_R^{-1})kappa(M_R), u_m eta_R kappa(M_R), and u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R, up to c(n,k) and omitted second-order terms. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17).)

The flexible bound has exactly the two displayed sources u_g kappa(AM_R^{-1})kappa(M_R) and u_a kappa(A)rho_A^R, up to c(n,k) and omitted second-order terms. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)
Flexible GMRES in this paper uses a fixed, not iteration-varying, right preconditioner. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, paragraph following Algorithm 1; PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, opening of Section 3.4.)

rho_A^R must be formed from the computed hat{Z}_k and computed hat{y}_k using the exact ratio in equation (3.15), not replaced silently by 1, kappa(M_R), or a generic constant. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)

The u_m term is removed from the flexible displayed error bound specifically because flexible solution formation does not reapply M_R^{-1}. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Remark 4; PDF p. 45, printed p. 44, equation (D.2).)

Removal of the explicit u_m term from (3.20) does not remove u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) or the other u_m-dependent quantities from the assumed condition (3.16). (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.16); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4 and Remark 5.)
The error notion is relative 2-norm forward error in x, and the claims do not provide a backward-error or residual bound. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, equation (2.1) and opening of Section 3.)

The final relations are lesssim bounds with unspecified c(n,k) and omitted second-order terms, not exact equalities or fully quantified numerical inequalities. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, notation convention; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)

ambiguities.issue: The norm underlying each unqualified kappa in (3.16), (3.17), and (3.20) is not uniquely selected.
ambiguities.evidence: The paper defines kappa_F, kappa_2, and kappa_{F,2} and then says it often writes only kappa(B) because the 2- and Frobenius-norm quantities are equivalent; the theorem formulas use this generic kappa notation. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.16)-(3.17).)
ambiguities.impact: A formal statement must either preserve an abstract/generic condition number or explicitly justify a particular norm choice; silently choosing kappa_2 or kappa_F strengthens the paper beyond its notation.

ambiguities.issue: The symbols << and lesssim and the polynomial c(n,k) are qualitative rather than numerically quantified.
ambiguities.evidence: Section 2 describes c(n,k) only as a low-degree polynomial and defines lesssim through dropping negligible second-order terms; equations (3.16), (3.17), and (3.20) provide no threshold, coefficient, or remainder. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.16)-(3.17); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)
ambiguities.impact: The source does not determine an exact epsilon threshold, an exact universal constant, or a closed-form remainder.

ambiguities.issue: The textual quantifier order for k is not fully formalized.
ambiguities.evidence: rho_A^R is defined using k before Theorem 3.3, condition (3.16) uses rho_A^R, and only afterward the theorem says there exists an iteration k <= n; Appendix C ties the witness to the existential iteration supplied by Theorem 3.1. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.15)-(3.17); PDF p. 44, printed p. 43, conclusion of Appendix C.)
ambiguities.impact: The text does not explicitly distinguish between a condition required for every candidate k, a condition evaluated at the eventual witness k, or existence of a k satisfying both the condition and bound. A formalization should preserve this issue rather than silently reorder the quantifiers.

ambiguities.issue: The ratio defining rho_A^R has an unstated nonzero-denominator requirement, and the vertical-bar notation is not separately defined in the selected notation section.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.15) displays rho_A^R = || |hat{Z}_k||hat{y}_k| ||_2/||hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k||_2 without an explicit assumption that the denominator is nonzero or a separate definition of |.|. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.15).)
ambiguities.impact: The conventional reading is componentwise absolute value, but the ratio is undefined when hat{Z}_k hat{y}_k = 0; neither point should be repaired silently.

ambiguities.issue: eta_R is intentionally generic and has no formula or universal bound in the selected result.
ambiguities.evidence: The text following (3.14) only calls eta_R a scalar quantifying the magnitude of the application error. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.14) and following sentence.)
ambiguities.impact: eta_R cannot faithfully be set to 1 or eliminated without an additional assumption about how the preconditioner is represented and applied.

ambiguities.issue: Remark 4's phrase that flexible preconditioning removes dependence on u_m applies directly to the displayed attainable-error bound, but not literally to all theorem hypotheses.
ambiguities.evidence: Equation (3.20) has no explicit u_m term, while Theorem 3.4 assumes all of (3.16), which includes u_m eta_R kappa(M_R); Remark 5 expressly discusses that retained requirement. (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.16); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4 and Remarks 4-5.)
ambiguities.impact: The source supports omission of u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) from the flexible conclusion, not an unconditional claim that applicability or all intermediate quantities are independent of u_m.

ambiguities.issue: The treatment of the initial guess is not reconciled explicitly between Algorithm 1 and the modular analysis.
ambiguities.evidence: Algorithm 1 displays r_0 = Ax_0-b and x_k = x_0 plus a correction, whereas Algorithm 2 writes the approximation as x_k = tilde{Z}_k y_k without displaying x_0. (PDF p. 4, printed p. 3, Algorithm 1, lines 1-18; PDF p. 7, printed p. 6, Algorithm 2, line 4.)
ambiguities.impact: The selected theorem does not specify whether the modular variable is a shifted correction or whether x_0 is specialized. A formal algorithmic reconstruction should record this mismatch rather than infer a sign or initial-guess convention.

contract_plain_english: For the mixed-precision right-preconditioned MGS-GMRES path, assume the normwise preconditioner-application model (3.14), the exact cancellation ratio rho_A^R from (3.15), and every one of the five smallness requirements in (3.16); then the paper claims only that some iteration k <= n attains the three-source relative 2-norm forward-error bound (3.17). (PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equations (3.14)-(3.17) and Theorem 3.3.) For the fixed-preconditioner flexible variant, the same model and full condition are retained, but the computed preconditioned basis is stored and used directly, so some k <= n attains (3.20), which omits the additive u_m eta_R kappa(M_R) reapplication term while retaining the u_g and u_a rho_A^R terms. (PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, Theorem 3.4, equation (3.20), and Remark 4; PDF p. 45, printed p. 44, equation (D.2).) Both are qualitative first-order attainable bounds with unspecified c(n,k), generic normwise kappa notation, and omitted second-order terms, not exact all-iteration guarantees. (PDF p. 6, printed p. 5, Section 2; PDF p. 11, printed p. 10, equation (3.17); PDF p. 12, printed p. 11, equation (3.20).)
